summary: Differentiate between a liquidity sweep and a liquidity run by observing the reaction to the Fair Value Gap that pushed price into the liquidity. A sweep disrespects this FVG and forms a reversal pattern (ST model) targeting opposing liquidity, while a run respects the FVG overlapping the broken level and continues the trend.

timeframes.notes: The strategy is fractal. The presenter demonstrates using a 4H chart for the higher timeframe draw on liquidity and a 15m chart for the entry model.

other: A clear Draw on Liquidity (e.g., a daily/weekly premium or discount array, or opposing liquidity pools).

glossary.Sweep: Price takes liquidity (a high/low) and immediately reverses toward opposing liquidity, disrespecting the FVG that initiated the move.
glossary.Run: Price takes a high/low and continues in that direction, respecting the FVG that overlaps with the recently taken liquidity level.
glossary.ST Model: A volatility-based reversal model that leaves behind inefficiencies (FVGs) to the opposite side, indicating huge institutional orders.
glossary.Sting: A shallow retracement into only the first available FVG, purposefully avoiding deeper overlapping PD arrays. Occurs when price is close to the ultimate draw on liquidity.
glossary.Overlapping PD Array: A PD array (like an FVG) that physically overlaps with a structural level, such as the high or low that was just broken.

sequence: Identify price moving into a higher timeframe premium/discount array or sweeping a liquidity level.
Observe the specific Fair Value Gap that was responsible for pushing price into this level.
If the FVG is completely rebalanced/disrespected and an ST model forms in the opposite direction, it is a Sweep. Enter the reversal targeting opposing liquidity.
If the FVG overlapping the taken level is respected and price stumbles/slowly continues away from it, it is a Run. Enter on the retracement to ride the expansion.

If price has already had a huge expansion and is close to the ultimate draw on liquidity, do not wait for a deep retracement into an overlapping array. Expect only a 'sting' into the first FVG before continuation.

invalidation.text: When expecting a 'run' on liquidity, an immediate full rebalance (disrespect) of the overlapping Fair Value Gap invalidates the run and suggests a sweep.

filters.text: Do not expect a deep retracement into an overlapping PD array if price is relatively close to the ultimate draw on liquidity.

entry_rule.text: Enter on the retracement into the newly formed Fair Value Gap of the ST model (for a sweep), or on the retracement into the overlapping Fair Value Gap (for a run/sting).
entry_rule.quote: we have an immediate retracement into that fair value Gap and we are slowly climbing higher right there and that right there is your SD entry

target_rule.text: For a sweep, target opposing liquidity (e.g., from buy-side liquidity to sell-side equal lows). For a run, target the ultimate draw on liquidity.
target_rule.quote: price will Target opposing liquidity buy side liquidity to now sell side liquidity

A bullish ST model forms on the 15-minute timeframe, confirming the sweep. The draw on liquidity shifts to the opposing equal highs.
Price begins to run highs. Because it is a run, it respects the FVGs overlapping with the taken highs and slowly climbs higher.

Because price has had a huge expansion and is now close to the ultimate draw on liquidity, it stops giving deep retracements to overlapping arrays and instead gives shallow 'stings' into the first available FVG before continuing higher.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Price sweeps a low, disrespects the bearish FVG that pushed it there, and forms a bullish ST model (Sweep).
Price breaks above a prior high, forming a bullish FVG overlapping the broken high. Price retraces into it and rejects higher (Run).
The process repeats. Price breaks another high, creates another ST-like structure, and respects the FVG overlapping the newly broken high.
As price approaches the ultimate draw on liquidity, it no longer makes a deep retracement, but instead just 'stings' a mitigation block overlapping a fair value gap before hitting the target.

presenter_commentary: He notes ES perfectly illustrates this cycle: sweep the low (disrespecting FVG), then consecutively run highs (respecting overlapping FVGs) until getting very close to the draw, where it only stings the first PD array before completion.

may_differ.reason: Traidle calculates if an FVG is mitigated, but does not natively require the FVG's zone to physically overlap the exact price of a recently broken structural event (BOS/liquidity sweep).
